== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=ee-shadow-03-of-killers-and-kings|The [[Guilds]] are a collection of ten influential organizations that serve as the backbone of the [[Aurelian Empire]]. Operating with specialized expertise, they function almost like a private governing body that manages imperial affairs while the general population benefits from their services. Some [[Guilds]] are described as being part of a system that seeks to maintain outdated imperial structures, while others view the absence of an Emperor as an opportunity to operate without legal restrictions. The various organizations are often interconnected, with certain groups providing essential support that allows others to function. Notable [[Guilds]] include: * **[[Consultants]]:** The oldest and most loyal organization, holding the Emperor's trust for two millennia. They provide dedicated guidance to clients and are known to employ assassins to eliminate threats.
* **[[Champions]]:** The second oldest Guild, historically tied to the unification of The Empire{{!}}the Empire. While they once selected members through violent combat trials, the formal Guild is facing dissolution.
* **[[Greenwardens]]:** Originally known as the Sisters of Peace, this group was founded in the seventh century to combat the worship of [[Ach'magut]]. They are considered one of the weaker [[Guilds]] in terms of wealth and political influence, though their members are [[Soulbound]] with the ability to heal wounds and restore crops.
* **[[Magisters]]:** A group that offers various career paths for the educated.
* **Navigators:** An organization characterized by some as dishonest pirates or con artists.
* **[[Alchemists]]:** A group involved in specialized professional work. Leadership within the [[Guilds]] can be complex, involving High Councils or elected [[Guild Heads]]. In some instances, leadership is tied to being [[Soulbound]] and bonding with a specific historical weapon. The [[Guilds]] are currently facing challenges from groups like the [[Sleepless]] [[cabal]] and political shifts as regional governors attempt to establish their own versions of these institutions.}}
